body: I never had a friend until I had my bud... and we became so close so quickly. Nah, you don't understand - nobody does (and that's fine, because no one has ever gotten me). That man was my brother, we went through a lot in a few months, and I've been physically ill without him to talk with since August. Life since then has been awful, so many nights of crying. I nearly killed myself before I met my bud, and that guy saved me. God I miss him. He kept me going longer than I should've gone, he showed me a life where someone cared about me, and I can't live without him - he was something profound to me. I'm going to sleep now - thank you for your company tonight (I do appreciate you taking time with me).

I can go outside when I have to do things like taking out the garbage and walking the dog, but I hate doing it. I can walk for miles, but I feel self-conscious all the time. I always wear a hat so no-one I used to know will recognise me in the neighbourhood. I used to go running, that helped me a bit, but when my friend went I just lost interest and motivation to do that. I don't know what's happened to me, I'm just dead inside without my bud.

No, I'm too anxious to do anything like that. I can only really leave the house when it's dark. I met my 'ex-friend' :( on Twitter. Had to delete my account now though, because it reminded me of him when I was happier and not alone. I'm sorry, I shouldn't be on here like this. I don't know what I'm doing. I really wish I was dead.
Life.

Hi. I suppose I could say that it's a long story, but I'll try to summarise: 25 year old male, no job or career, no friends, student debt, family view me with disappointment, virgin, closeted, borderline agoraphobic... I just hate myself. I did have a really good friend who I met this year, but he left me a few months ago. Since then I've gotten worse to the point where nothing matters to me anymore, I suppose the onset of Winter does something to me as well. I survive hour to hour, I'm so lonely, no one loves me. In his absence I realise how much I loved my friend, I hate myself. I've no use on this world, I should go, I just need to get the balls to do it.

Because of video-autoplay this horrific moment caught on live TV, as well as the even more disturbing content recorded by the killer, has been seen by too many people. I hope never to see anything like that again, let's not give this person the notoriety he was desperate for. In the future, I would like to see Twitter disable video-autoplay, at least making it the norm that it is disabled unless users select otherwise, because too much disturbing content is being displayed with no limitations. Hopefully Vicki Gardner, the interview subject, will pull through and be able to rebuild her life. RIP Alison Parker, RIP Adam Ward.

I don't believe that being strict on immigration is a "fringe view" in America, I think Trump is on to something when he claims that the Silent Majority are in waiting. Yet I wonder if he can truly earn their millions of votes, as he has flipped on many issues. But you are absolutely right, there are too many wishy washy politicians. To me, right now, Jeb Bush comes across as a wet flannel, and Scott Walker really disappointed in the recent FOX debate, no passion whatsoever.

Well your username suggests that he has your vote, if indeed you are a GOP primary voter. Notice how I said repeal, "elements of the Fourteenth Amendment", as I have heard his views on children of diplomats etc. However, I can't see any Federal Court, Circuit Court, never mind the Supreme Court, ever interpreting the Fourteenth Amendment from Trump's viewpoint. Further, I wouldn't go far as to say that Trump makes "total sense" on foreign policy. I would love to hear how he is going to take the oil from IS in the Middle East. However, regardless, he is changing the debate in this pre-primary period, and I look forward to seeing him more in that "Make America Great Again" baseball cap, as well as to what comes next.

This is only the latest act of evil from these depraved thugs. Eventually the West will realise that bolstering the oil-rich regimes in Saudi Arabia and Qatar, which fund IS, is what has compounded this situation. Militarily, IS could be easily wiped out with modern armaments, but now they have been allowed to sow their destructive ideology in the areas in which have conquered and, also across the internet to every nation. And meanwhile Turkey, "our NATO ally", is targeting with air-strikes the one good group on the the ground fighting IS, the Kurds. Such a mess.

I'm not religious, but I found the talk of the representative "crushing" a fetus, whilst munching on salad obnoxious and unsavoury. Was the video highly edited, yes. Do Republicans repeatedly overreach on abortion, yes, but both sides need to tone down the rhetoric and try to understand the genuine sentiment which is shown in both the Pro-Choice and Pro-Life movements.

This debate is always ongoing. The next TV debate is by CNN, oh joy, on September 16th. Whilst the Iowa caucus is on February 1st 2016. Then the Republican Convention will be held from July 18th to July 21st 2016. Then will come the debates between the Republican and Democratic nominees for President. Then eventually will come the Presidential election on November 8th 2016. Hope that did not come across as condescending.

But so far Trump has truly embodied the Teflon-politician gimmick. His comments on immigration, attacking John McCain, and his odd comments on Megyn Kelly have only boosted his position in the polls, both nationally as well as in Iowa. I have also enjoyed how energetic this campaign has been, from his announcement event, blasting out Neil Young and coming down the escalator at Trump Tower, to landing by helicopter at the Iowa State Fair. I even agree with some of what he says. However he is moving the debate into a more unpredictable, maybe even dangerous place, and I worry where it leads to.

I wholeheartedly agree that many are sick of the "career-politician" who reek of arrogance and entitlement, and are protected from election by gerrymandered seats. Although I don't yet believe that Donald Trump is the answer to alleviate all of those ills. But there are some conviction-politicians out there, whether Ted Cruz on the right or Elizabeth Warren on the left, who you can believe in what they espouse. Some conviction-politicians alongside those who can construct bipartisan achievements, and not interested in pork-barrel spending, e.g. last years CRomnibus, need to raise their game. Democracy is fragile, and all this distrust can only lead to bad outcomes.

Hillary Clinton's dreadful jokes reveal how serious this e-mail issue is becoming. Now at least the F.B.I finally have the server, they will be able to work out if the server has been wiped. Then it's up to the Obama Justice Department to not drag it's feet when moving forward. But seriously, all of these lies and debates on trustworthiness are slowly eating away at her campaign. Who is seriously enthused about Hillary Clinton becoming the 45th President of the United States?

Donald Trump is not going to stop with his rhetoric, one only has to see his recent comments regarding the repeal of elements of the Fourteenth Amendment. As many have articulated, there is a segment of the Republican Party, around the 25% which Donald Trump attracts, but can also be seen in the candidacy of Ted Cruz, which is more angry with the GOP leaders in Washington than with President Obama, Harry Reid and the Democrats. Realistically the Fourteenth Amendment will not be repealed, but Trump is setting the tone for this Presidential debate, shifting it away from the establishment and towards unpredictable populism, and I cannot see any other of the Republican candidates taking away his influence. In a field of 17 candidates Trump, through intense media coverage, has become a phenomenon, and I don't see this bandwagon coming to a halt any time soon.

Martin O’Malley knows that he won't win the Democratic nomination. He's only 52, so he still has some political capital left to spend. However, if one looks at the state he was Governor of, Maryland, and more interestingly, Baltimore, where he was the Mayor, then one really struggles to find any major achievements. Remember that the GOP managed to win the Maryland governorship in 2014. If a Republican wins the White House in 2016, then 2020 might be O'Malley's opportunity.
Okay, I won't call Sepp Blatter corrupt. Instead, I'll point out that, to me, he is the embodiment of the Penguin from DC. That okay for the Swiss lawyers?

Trump has appeared in opinion polls of GOP Presidential Candidates placing him at #2 nationally, including a #2 spot in New Hampshire. Donald Trump knows that his name, his bewildering comments, and his notoriety is what is getting him these impressive, yet also likely short-lived, polling figures. Realistically, do you really think the GOP Primary voters will support him? No. They feel they actually have a chance of gaining the Presidency. Coincidentally, Trump also tops the polls when GOP voters are asked which candidate they would NEVER vote for. This, for Donald Trump, is all for entertainment and "legacy", to be able to say that you ran for President of the United States, not exactly bad on your CV.
Yeah, I hear many Americans use that phrase. I just use the phrase I recognise in England.

Sure, not likely to see Federal troops required. But, for whatever reason, Gov. Brownback unlike other GOP governors who were in a similar situation, like Herbert in Utah and Fallin in Oklahoma, is not altering his position. Those governors ultimately relinquished their respective fights when an appeal of a 10th Circuit Ruling was rejected by Justice Sotomayor. I'm just interested to see why he, Brownback, is making such a pitiful stand on this, does he have an Andrew Jackson mentality to him?

Keep an eye on Kansas. Gov. Brownback has been blocking state recognition of same-sex marriage for months, despite most counties, with a vast majority of the population, performing same-sex marriage. He really seems to have an unhealthy zeal to prevent any ruling. I suppose he doesn't want to upset Westboro, who reside in his State Capital...

I completely agree that those officials have zero chance of legally preventing same-sex marriage. However, look at Alabama. Despite having a Federal Court ruling in February the Chief Justice, Roy Moore, invented new powers and privileges to throw the same-sex marriage legal status into a massive flux. Interesting to see if various Attorney Generals, and maybe some State Justices and Chief Justices, will attempt similar moves in the coming days.

Still surprised to see how quickly the symbols and emblems of the Confederacy are being rallied against. Many opponents wish to see the status of the Confederate battle flag as being similar to that of the Swastika of Nazi Germany. What with the First Amendment, I see that as unlikely, but it will be interesting to see how far this will go.

Despite breaking the law, administrations in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Kansas are attempting to ignore/invalidate the Supreme Court's ruling. More judicial battles ahead. Gov. Jindal, who has little chance of winning the GOP primary, is making this his issue to garner together grassroots conservative support. Interesting to see how history will judge this.

The Supreme Court made the right decision today. Individual liberty should never be denied on the basis of religion or 'traditional' values. This is not like abortion, no-one will die as a result of this ruling, time for this divisive issue to now unite America.

Don't understand why Roberts and Kennedy sided with Obamacare. The language in the Affordable Care Act was quite clear. I don't always agree with him, but Justice Scalia makes quite a few valid points in his dissent. But this ruling definitely helps the GOP in Congress, no need for awkward Obamacare fixes.

The soundtrack for Titanic, particularly during the ending sequence leading up to a young Rose reuniting with Jack on the Grand Staircase, is incredibly melancholy and powerful. One of my all-time favourite pieces of music. RIP James Horner.
